name: DyBASE
tagline: Konstantin Knizhnik's tiny embedded object database for dynamically typed languages like Python, Ruby and PHP.
description: DyBASE is a small embedded object-oriented database by Konstantin Knizhnik, author of FastDB, GigaBASE and GOODS, first released in 2003. It targets languages with dynamic typing (PHP, Python, Ruby and Rebol), where an instance variable can hold an integer one moment and an object reference the next, so it stores a type tag with every field instead of relying on class descriptors. Applications persist their own objects directly, with no mapping layer, special compiler or preprocessor, and still get ACID transactions and concurrent access. Its best-known downstream use was as the persistence layer for TIScript, the scripting language of the Sciter UI engine. Development stopped at version 0.22; it remains a neat reference design rather than something to adopt.
statusNote: No updates for well over a decade (last download 0.22 on garret.ru); the author's later work moved to PostgreSQL and other projects.
queryLanguages: Native language API (PHP, Python, Ruby, Rebol)
strengths: Persists dynamic-language objects directly, with per-field type tags instead of a fixed schema
ACID transactions in a tiny embeddable library
No preprocessor or code generation step
weaknesses: Unmaintained for over a decade; language bindings target old PHP, Python and Ruby versions
No query language, so lookups are written by hand in application code
useCases: Studying object persistence for dynamically typed languages
Maintaining legacy TIScript/Sciter-era applications that use it
